question: In QLoRA, distinguish the usual weight storage dtype, computation dtype, and which parameters receive weight gradients.

candidate_claims.text: QLoRA stores weights in 4-bit NormalFloat and computes in 16-bit BrainFloat. It computes gradients only for the LoRA parameters.

To summarize, QLoRA has one storage data type (usually 4-bit NormalFloat) and a computation data type (16-bit BrainFloat).
